messages:
sara_support: FYI — Ryan from Zenith reporting a spike of 429s hitting their dedicated pool (pool-id: rp-zenith-03) starting ~03:40 UTC. Logs show repeated "quota_exceeded" with X-RateLimit headers at 0. Pasting sample response:

ryan_customer: here's the curl and response I got:
```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Tenant: zenith-corp' \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 60
{"error":"quota_exceeded"}
```

sara_support: added logs + tenant id to this thread, escalated to eng. Customer says this started after a plan-sync last night.

eli_eng: thanks — can you paste the tenant quota config we have in the billing system? also need autoscaler logs around 03:35-03:50 UTC.

ops_oncall: I see an autoscale alert from autoscale-bot at 03:36 that the reserved pool flagged as quietpool; scale-up suppressed due to min_instance_pin. Posting excerpt from autoscale-bot: 

```
[autoscale-bot] 03:36:12 WARN pool=rp-zenith-03 scale_action=NOOP reason=min_pin_active current_instances=2 target=6 min_instance_pin=2 warmup_block=true
```

maria_sre: warmup_block=true looks suspicious. If the warmup flag is stuck we won't let new instances handle traffic until prefix caches warm — combined with a low-per-tenant ceiling you'll hit 429s. Can you pull the quota record?

sara_support: quota record from billing-db (sanitized):
```yaml
tenant: zenith-corp
plan: reserved-gold
per_minute_units: 60
per_hour_units: 3600
min_instance_pin: 2
warmup_disabled: true  # set during last migration
prefix_cache_ttl_seconds: 900
```

eli_eng: aha — warmup_disabled: true + min_instance_pin means scaler won't route live traffic to newly created instances until a manual override. Also per_minute_units at 60 looks like it's been artificially reduced during plan conversion (was supposed to be 600). That mismatch means the tenant gets starved while pool-level capacity exists.

ops_oncall: repro steps I've been using locally:
```bash
# simulate tenant traffic at ~1.5x configured rate
for i in {1..150}; do 
  curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Tenant: zenith-corp' -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done; wait
# observe 429s and headers
```

eli_eng: suggested mitigation: temporarily bump per_minute_units to 600 and flip warmup_disabled to false OR set a per-tenant override that routes to dedicated reserve (force-route) while we roll a migration fix. Also issue a one-off scale-up to 8 instances to absorb burst.

maria_sre: I'm applying the temporary override now (will document change). Also disabling min_instance_pin so scale-up can attach traffic immediately. I'll keep warmup flag unchanged until we confirm prefix cache behaviour.

autoscale-bot: [03:58:01 INFO] pool=rp-zenith-03 action=scale target_instances=8 initiated_by=maria_sre

sara_support: told Ryan we were rolling a fix and applied a temporary override, offered 24h credit for the impacted window. Ryan: any update?

ryan_customer: thanks, saw errors drop immediately after ~03:59. Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm root cause & permanent fix.

eli_eng: root cause summary for support note: plan-migration script set per_minute_units to the wrong denom (factor of 0.1) and enabled warmup_disabled during migration. Combined with min_instance_pin this prevented autoscaler from routing to new instances, causing per-tenant throttling despite pool capacity.

eli_eng: next steps: 1) roll migration script fix and re-run for affected tenants, 2) add a validation that rejects warmup_disabled on active dedicated pools, 3) add alerts when X-RateLimit-Remaining hits 0 while pool has spare capacity.

maria_sre: filing postmortem action items and assigning owners. I'll update this thread when the migration re-run is scheduled.

sara_support: closing loop with Ryan, adding credits + note. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
